assessment.subject: spontaneous neural activity in human and mouse cortical organoids (MEA recordings)
assessment.claim_summary: Persistent homology detects significant loop (H1) topological structure above a matched null in 14 of 18 organoid MEA datasets, with H2 emerging only in larger networks.
assessment.magnitude: H1 above null in 14/18 datasets; 26-234 units

assessment.subject: transient bimodality in stochastic dynamical systems
assessment.claim_summary: A minimal theoretical model yields a general criterion for transient bimodality, showing fast-to-slow (not only slow-to-fast) dynamics can produce it.

assessment.subject: conscious systems / motivated behavior
assessment.claim_summary: Proposes the Positive Experience Principle: conscious systems inherently tend toward higher positive subjective experience, quantified by a scalar PEV derived from an earlier consciousness theory.

assessment.subject: cooperation in public goods games with frequency-dependent returns
assessment.claim_summary: Theory (verified by individual-based simulation) shows whether cooperation is favored depends solely on the investment return rate in the full-contribution state of the group.

assessment.subject: excitation energy transfer network of Photosystem II core pigments
assessment.claim_summary: A network built from Forster EET rates in cyanobacterial PSII reproduces known functional roles of pigments, indicating topology encodes functionally relevant information.

assessment.subject: EEG/MEG-based brain network analysis methods
assessment.claim_summary: A methodological review/book chapter surveying EEG/MEG brain-network analysis: forward/inverse problems, source reconstruction, connectivity measures, pipelines, and emerging approaches.

assessment.subject: polyploidy / genome redundancy in evolution
assessment.claim_summary: A minimal evolutionary model finds polyploidy is especially advantageous during abrupt environmental change, with inheritance mode and genotype-phenotype mapping shaping the optimal ploidy level.

assessment.subject: machine-learning prediction of DNA-binding protein binding free energy
assessment.object: PU.1 transcription factor sliding on mammalian chromosomes
assessment.claim_summary: A machine-learning model trained on protein-DNA structures and measured binding energies predicts genome-wide binding free-energy profiles, applied to map PU.1 binding regions and stability.

assessment.subject: dengue transmission dynamics
assessment.object: finite hospital capacity and threshold-based fogging interventions
assessment.claim_summary: A non-smooth ODE dengue model shows hospital capacity and reactive fogging create distinct operating regimes and bifurcations, and identifies locally optimal intervention thresholds.

assessment.subject: missing-data/imputation methods for average treatment effect estimation
assessment.object: MICE vs hot-deck vs single-mode imputation vs complete-case under time-varying confounding
assessment.claim_summary: A simulation study finds multiple imputation (MICE) generally achieves better coverage and lower bias than other missing-data methods under time-varying confounding.

assessment.subject: conditional randomization test with external/unlabeled data (CRT*)
assessment.claim_summary: CRT* integrates heterogeneous external/unlabeled data to maintain type-I error control and achieve strictly higher power than standard CRT, supported by theory, simulations, and RNA-seq analysis.

assessment.subject: path-signature features for path regression
assessment.claim_summary: Establishes a minimax-optimal L2 approximation rate for signature-based path regression and consistency for three estimators, with three real-data applications improving prediction over handcrafted features.

assessment.subject: Bayesian joint model of tumour growth and time-to-event endpoints (PIONEER)
assessment.object: extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer trials; mature Kaplan-Meier curves
assessment.claim_summary: A Bayesian mechanistic joint model produces calibrated PFS/OS forecasts from immature oncology-trial data, giving at least 8 months of advance forecasting with quantified uncertainty (N=497).

assessment.subject: time-sensitive importance splitting for rare-event simulation
assessment.claim_summary: Proposes timer resampling and global-age pruning for time-sensitive importance splitting, yielding a distance-metric taxonomy and experimentally improved estimator accuracy.

assessment.subject: privacy-preserving federated causal mediation analysis (GLP-1 -> HbA1c via BMI)
assessment.claim_summary: A federated mediation estimator reproduces pooled-data results without sharing patient records; across 32,146 EHR patients, BMI mediated only a small proportion of GLP-1's HbA1c reduction.
assessment.magnitude: small proportion of total effect mediated by BMI

assessment.subject: Bayesian Conway-Maxwell-Poisson model with spike-and-slab priors for dispersed counts
assessment.object: standard Poisson model; English Premier League goal data
assessment.claim_summary: A Bayesian CMP model with spike-and-slab dispersion priors captures under/over-dispersion and improves fit and predictive performance over the Poisson model on Premier League scores.

assessment.subject: rage intensity and facial gestures in human driving
assessment.claim_summary: A Bayesian network with beta-distributed nodes finds brow lowering strongly associated with rage (more frequent in men) and upper-lid raising decreasing under provocation, and predicts rage from gestures.
assessment.magnitude: brow lowering strongly associated with rage; more frequent in men

assessment.subject: binomial-like heavy-tailed discrete distribution
assessment.claim_summary: Introduces a heavy-tailed binomial-like distribution as a weighted mixture of the binomial and a new bi-uniform pmf, derives its properties, and demonstrates fit to a classical dataset.
